title: The Cosmic Dipole Anomaly as Regime-Dependent Anisotropy in Energy-Flow Cosmology
description: Working note that proposes a natural EFC mechanism for the excess galaxy number-count dipole (2–3× kinematic). In EFC, large-scale isotropy is a regime condition; a residual super-Hubble entropy gradient ∇S modulates the effective coupling G_eff(S) and thus structure growth, yielding a dipole aligned with the CMB but with amplified amplitude. The note derives the leading-order dipole, estimates the required ~2% entropy gradient, and states falsifiable predictions and open gaps.

G_eff.description: In EFC, the effective gravitational coupling depends on the entropy field S via an enhancement function f(S) with calibration amplitude \mu_0.

directional_G_eff.latex: \Delta G_{\rm eff}(\hat{n}) \simeq G_N\, \mu_0\, f'(\bar S)\, (\nabla S \cdot \hat{n})\, L_{\rm grad}
directional_G_eff.description: A large-scale entropy gradient induces a directional modulation of G_eff across the sky with coherence scale L_grad.

fractional_excess_counts.latex: \frac{\delta N}{N}(\hat{n}) \simeq b_{\rm eff} \, \frac{\partial \ln \sigma_8}{\partial \ln G_{\rm eff}} \, \frac{\Delta G_{\rm eff}(\hat{n})}{G_N}
fractional_excess_counts.description: Leading-order fractional change in number counts from direction-dependent growth; in the linear regime \sigma_8 \propto G_{\rm eff}^{1/2}.

dipole_amplitude.latex: D_{\rm EFC} \simeq \frac{b_{\rm eff}}{2} \, \mu_0 \, \lvert f'(\bar S)\rvert \, \frac{\lvert\nabla S\rvert \, L_{\rm grad}}{\bar S}
dipole_amplitude.description: Predicted EFC contribution to the number-count dipole from a super-Hubble entropy gradient.

required_gradient.latex: \frac{\lvert\nabla S\rvert \, L_{\rm grad}}{\bar S} \simeq 0.023 \quad (\text{for } D_{\rm excess} \simeq 0.007,\ b_{\rm eff}\!\approx\!1.5,\ \mu_0\!=\!0.415,\ \lvert f'(\bar S)\rvert\!\sim\!1)
required_gradient.description: Order-of-magnitude entropy gradient across the observable volume needed to explain the observed dipole excess.

key_results.main_finding: EFC naturally yields an intrinsic number-count dipole via a super-Hubble entropy gradient modulating G_eff(S), with the observed excess explained by an O(2%) gradient across the survey volume.

sealed_predictions.statement: Dipole excess increases toward lower redshift (intrinsic component grows with decreasing z), unlike the redshift-independent kinematic dipole.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Tomographic number-count dipole measurements showing no increase toward low z across multiple tracers after controlling systematics.

sealed_predictions.statement: Directional anisotropy in growth, fσ8, at ~2% level aligned with the number-count dipole.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: DESI/Euclid directional fσ8 constraints below ~0.5–1% in the dipole direction across 0.2 < z < 1 without corresponding signal.

sealed_predictions.statement: Dipole direction approximately aligns with CMB dipole and bulk-flow measurements, with amplitude exceeding pure kinematic prediction.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Joint analyses showing alignment breaks (e.g., >30° misalignment) or amplitude fully consistent with kinematic value after robust systematics control.

sealed_predictions.statement: Scale dependence: excess is stronger for tracers that probe larger volumes (k ≲ 0.01 Mpc⁻¹).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Multi-tracer, multi-scale studies finding no increase of dipole amplitude with survey depth/volume or large-scale mode weighting.

kill_criteria: KC1: Tomographic number-count dipole across independent tracers (radio, IR, optical) is fully consistent with the kinematic prediction (D ≈ 0.0045) at all redshifts 0 < z < 2 within ±10%, leaving no residual intrinsic component > 0.001.

KC2: Directional growth measurements constrain anisotropy in fσ8 below 0.5% (95% CL) along the observed dipole/CMB direction over 0.1 < z < 1, ruling out the ~2% modulation required by the EFC mechanism.

KC3: A rigorous multi-tracer aberration/Doppler analysis demonstrates that the observed dipole is entirely explained by observer motion after controlling for flux/calibration systematics, leaving D_excess < 0.001 (95% CL).

KC4: CMB large-scale isotropy and ISW/lensing cross-correlation bounds exclude any super-Hubble entropy (or equivalent potential) gradient at the level (|∇S| L_grad / S̄) ≥ 0.01, inconsistent with the ~0.02 required by EFC.

KC5: Independent calibration shows f'(S̄) ≈ 0 near the L1→L2 regime transition or a value of μ0 incompatible with SPARC (e.g., μ0 < 0.05 at 95% CL), eliminating sufficient coupling sensitivity to generate the dipole.
KC6: The inferred dipole direction is robustly misaligned (>45°) with both the CMB dipole and bulk-flow direction across tracers, contradicting the predicted alignment pattern.
abstract: Examines whether EFC contains a natural mechanism for the observed galaxy number count dipole excess (2-3x kinematic prediction). Identifies the key ingredient: isotropy is a regime condition valid in L0/L1, not an absolute postulate. Any residual entropy gradient ∇S imprints a preferred direction via G_eff(S). Required gradient is ~2% across the observable volume, consistent with CMB constraints.

key_equations.directional_G_eff: ΔG_eff(n̂) ≈ G_N μ₀ f'(S̄) (∇S · n̂) L_grad

predictions.description: Redshift dependence: dipole excess grows with decreasing z
Alignment with bulk flow and CMB dipole direction
Scale dependence: excess stronger for large-volume tracers

open_gaps.description: Quantitative f(S) profile at super-Hubble scales
